selected_primary_scope_checks.title: A slightly improved upper bound for quantum statistical zero-knowledge
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: The improvement bounds the honest prover space in a two-message quantum protocol. It leaves the ordinary PSPACE upper bound in place; polynomial time in Hilbert-space dimension is exponential in its qubit encoding. No SZK⊆PP/BQP consequence.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Lattice Based Crypto breaks in a Superposition of Spacetimes
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: SZK⊆BQP^OI uses an order-interference oracle, a different computation model. It does not establish SZK⊆BQP.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Space-bounded quantum interactive proof systems
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: QIPL and QIP_UL restrict verifier space and intermediate measurements; QSZK_UL=BQL is not ordinary SZK or QSZK. NP⊆QIPL⊆SBP recovers a known roster inclusion.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: The Black-Box Simulation Barrier Persists in a Fully Quantum World
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Constant-round fully quantum black-box simulation with the specified expected-QPT notion implies membership in BQP. That protocol hypothesis is not supplied by ordinary SZK membership. The authors explicitly distinguish coherent-runtime simulation. No SZK⊆BQP or QMA⊆BQP follows.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Separating Quantum and Classical Advice with Good Codes
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Both QMA/QCMA and BQP/qpoly versus BQP/poly separations are relative to classical oracles. They are not ordinary class separations; advice endpoints also differ from P/poly.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: En Route to a Standard QMA1 vs. QCMA Oracle Separation
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Classical/in-place oracle constructions and bounded adaptivity; precise-gap variants. No ordinary QMA⊄QCMA theorem.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: QMA has perfect completeness
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Post-cutoff claim QMA=QMA1, excluded regardless of its validity. QMA1 is not a roster endpoint. This audit does not assess its proof.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Complexity Theory for Quantum Promise Problems
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: p/m classes use pure/mixed quantum states as inputs. Their unconditional separations do not transfer to this benchmark of total decision languages over finite bitstrings.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: On the Complexity of Unique Quantum Witnesses and Quantum Approximate Counting
selected_primary_scope_checks.locator: Abstract; full preprint arXiv:2410.23811; ITCS2026 publication Jan23
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Quantum-oracle separations concerning UniqueQMA and quantum approximate counting; no ordinary roster separation or collapse.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: On the Pure Quantum Polynomial Hierarchy and Quantified Hamiltonian Complexity
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: QMA(2)⊆pureQΣ2⊆QΣ3⊆NEXP and pureQPH=QPH concern quantum quantifier hierarchies, not the roster classical PH. QMA⊆NEXP is already known.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Unentanglement and Post-Measurement Branching in Quantum Interactive Proofs
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Three-round unentangled quantum interactive systems can capture NEXP. Restricting branching gives a QAM bound. Neither protocol class is ordinary QMA.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Quantum Merlin-Arthur with an Internally Separable Proof
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: A structural promise on proof-state separability changes the witness model. Its one-proof EXP upper bound and two-proof NEXP characterization do not show NEXP⊆ordinary QMA.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: MPC in the Quantum Head (or: Superposition-Secure (Quantum) Zero-Knowledge)
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Three-round arguments in the common reference string model, conditional on LWE. These are not unconditional statistical zero-knowledge proofs and give no QMA⊆SZK inclusion.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Bosonic Quantum Computational Complexity
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Continuous-variable, infinite-dimensional models have different resource bounds. Its BQP lower/EXPSPACE upper bounds for bosonic classes and Hamiltonian-specific classifications do not improve an ordinary roster relation.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: A complexity theory for non-local quantum computation
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Resource-efficient reductions between communication/entanglement tasks, not ordinary language class inclusions.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Spectral Gaps with Quantum Counting Queries and Oblivious State Preparation
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Numerical spectral estimation with QRAM/query costs and explicit dimension dependence. Quantum counting here is an algorithmic primitive, not a PP/#P class simulation.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: On the Computational Hardness of Quantum One-Wayness
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: A PP oracle can break one-way state generators; a bounded-copy unconditional construction does not establish an ordinary class separation. This paper originated before2024, but its recent journal version was screened.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Unconditional Quantum Advantage for Sampling with Shallow Circuits
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Unconditional separation is a sampling task against constant-depth bounded-fan-in classical circuits with randomness restrictions. It is not BQP⊄BPP or a decision-language AC0 claim.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: A brief history of quantum vs classical computational advantage
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Reviews experiments and selected algorithmic advantages. This is not a survey certifying all complexity-class relation statuses. Publication is exactly at the cutoff.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Quantum state synthesis: relation with decision complexity classes and impossibility of error reduction
selected_primary_scope_checks.locator: Theorem1 pp758–759; Propositions3–4 and Theorem2 pp759–760; Theorem3 p762
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Relational state-synthesis error separations concern different task/error parameters. Theorem2 supplies a conditional route to BQP≠QCMA; it does not establish that route’s premise. The unconditional error-reduction impossibility is not an unconditional BQP/QCMA separation.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Quantum SAT Problems with Finite Sets of Projectors Are Complete for a Plethora of Classes
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Different finite-projector restrictions yield different complete problems and new union/intersection classes. No equality or separation between ordinary roster classes is proved by this taxonomy.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Uniformity Testing When You Have the Source Code
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: The cost is polynomial in distribution domain size, not its succinct circuit input length. It does not place general succinct Statistical Difference or SZK in BQP.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Taming Quantum Time Complexity
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Removes overhead in quantum subroutine composition. It does not simulate arbitrary classical nondeterminism or counting in quantum polynomial time.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: The Complexity of Being Entangled
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Geodesic and binding complexity of state preparation, not a relation between decision complexity classes.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: On the quantum computational complexity of classical linear dynamics with geometrically local interactions: Dequantization and universality
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: Bounds concern dimension-dependent dynamics and exponential-time/polynomial-space quantum computation. The special-case dequantization is not BQP⊆BPP.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Lossy Cryptography from Code-Based Assumptions
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: A proposed code-based problem lies in BPP^SZK. Its assumed cryptographic hardness gives no unconditional SZK separation.

selected_primary_scope_checks.title: Perfect Zero-Knowledge PCPs for #P
selected_primary_scope_checks.scope: An oracle-access PCP and its local simulator are not an ordinary polynomial-communication SZK proof. No PP⊆SZK conclusion.
